title: Secret lifecycle matrix and SIEM mapping
content:
Purpose:
This document provides a concise operational runbook and classification matrix for all secret types used across Redwood Inference, plus a recommended SIEM mapping for audit events and evidence automation hooks. It is intended for on-call SREs, SecOps, and platform engineers who operate the Vault clusters, rotation jobs, and SIEM pipelines.

Scope:
- Secrets in scope: long-lived service credentials, short-lived ephemeral tokens, database credentials, SSH keys, signing keys, TLS private keys, third-party API keys, and machine identity certificates.
- Not in scope: user-facing passwords stored in 3rd-party SaaS (except where we keep copies), PII unrelated to secret access.

1) Secret classification matrix (high-level)
Columns: secret_type | example | confidentiality | rotation-frequency | storage | owner | emergency-flag
- service-account-key | GCP JSON key / AWS static creds | H | 24h (if ephemeral) / 90d (if static) | Vault (transit + kv-v2) | eng-platform | true
- db-admin-user | postgres admin user password | H | 7d | Vault kv-v2 with versioning | infra-database | true
- product-api-key | external payment provider | M | 30d | Vault kv-v2 + metadata (source) | integrations | false
- tls-private-key | cert private key for edge | H | 365d (rotation coordinated with CA) | HSM-backed Vault (if available) | infra-networking | true
- signing-key | internal model-signing key | H | 90d + rekey on personnel change | HSM or secure vault mount | applied-ml | true
- ephemeral-session-token | ephemeral token issued by STS | L | 0 (TTL-based) | not persisted server-side; ephemeral cache only | auth-service | false
Notes: H = high, M = medium, L = low. Emergency-flag indicates whether break-glass flows are permitted.

2) Vaulting & storage guidelines (patterns)
- Prefer kv-v2 for versioned storage of static secrets; enable max_versions and configure periodic pruning jobs.
- Use transit for signing/encryption operations; never export raw key materials from KMS/HSM-bound keys.
- HSM-backed keys mandatory for production TLS/private signing keys and any customer-sensitive encryption keys.
- Metadata: every KV entry must include: owner, team, jira_ticket, allowed_roles (RBAC-v2 group ids), last_rotation_ts, rotation_policy_id. This metadata is critical for automation and evidence generation.
- Access policy hygiene: use least privilege in Vault policies; map Vault policies to RBAC-v2 roles (see mapping table in appendix). Avoid large coarse-grained policies.

3) Rotation workflows (standard flow for non-emergency rotations)
Trigger: scheduled rotation job OR owner-initiated via playbook.
Pre-conditions:
- A runbook ticket exists (JIRA) with scope and rollback plan.
- Relevant consumers are known and have test harnesses.
Steps:
1. Create new secret version in Vault (kv-v2 create). Tag with rotation_job_id and set state to staging.
2. Run compatibility tests in staging environment (smoke requests to dependent services).
3. Update consumer service config to read new version (use version-aware fetch).
4. Gradually rollout using canary percentage (default 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on error thresholds.
5. After successful rollout and 24h observation window, mark previous versions for archival and set deletion_ttl per policy.
6. Emit evidence bundle: rotation_job_id, commit diff, test results, rollout percentages, final status. Persist bundle to evidence-bucket and append pointer to Vault metadata.
Automation hooks: rotation job should call the evidence automation endpoint (see linked_artifacts) to push structured JSON for audit and SIEM ingestion.

4) Emergency/Break-glass procedure (temporary tokens and remediation)
Use only when a secret is believed compromised and immediate containment is required.
Steps:
- Pager escalation: declare incident on-call -> create incident ticket -> notify infra-sec slack-#sec-ops.
- Short-lived workaround: issue a short-lived ephemeral token from a privileged vault role with TTL <= 1h for remediation tasks. Log issuance in audit with tag break_glass=true and include approver (Slack link or issuer id).
- Rotate compromised secret using the emergency rotation playbook: create replacement secret, update critical consumers in parallel (scripting recommended), monitor for failures.
- Post-incident: mandatory rekey of any roots/HSM material that may have been exposed; rotate downstream derived keys.
- Evidence: collect audit_log_ids, rotation_job_id, approver_slack_ids, and a snapshot of active sessions. Attach to incident ticket.
Guardrails:
- Break-glass tokens must be single-use and require at least one on-call approver (not the issuer) to be stamped in Slack or ticket system.
- All break-glass events auto-create a post-mortem check-in meeting scheduled within 48 hours.

5) RBAC-v2 mapping principles (summary)
- Map least-privilege roles to Vault policies via a canonical mapping table (role_id -> allowed_policies). Example roles: platform-deployer, infra-operator, sec-auditor, svc-account-reader.
- Admin scopes: only a small set of long-lived service principals hold unbounded policy updates; these actions require audit approval and MFA for UI/API actions.
- Temporary elevation: use ephemeral group membership with TTL and an approval ticket; all elevations logged in audit.

6) SIEM export & audit schema (recommended fields)
Event envelope fields (minimum): event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_id, actor_type (user/service), action, target_path, target_type, request_id, request_payload_hash, response_status, policy_eval (allowed/denied), rbacsnapshot (role ids active), rotation_job_id (optional), evidence_bundle_id (optional), break_glass (bool), approver_id (optional).
Suggested mapping examples:
- vault.kv.read -> action: secret_read | target_path: kv-v2/data/myapp/creds | policy_eval -> allowed
- vault.kv.create -> action: secret_write | include rotation_job_id in metadata when part of rotation flow
- vault.hsm.sign -> action: cryptographic_sign | target_type: transit-key | policy_eval -> allowed/denied
Notes: keep payloads small in SIEM — store hashes and pointers to evidence-bucket rather than full secrets.

7) Evidence automation (what to capture and how)
Minimum evidence capture per rotation or break-glass: rotation_job_id, initiator_id, approver_id(s), changed_paths[], version_before, version_after, test_results_url, rollout_timeline (timestamps), related_jira, related_incident_id.
- Evidence ingestion: rotation jobs post JSON to evidence-ingest API; service stores JSON to S3 with immutable object lock and returns evidence_bundle_id.
- SIEM pipeline pulls metadata (not secret contents) and indexes fields listed in audit schema for search and alerting.

8) Operational runbook snippets (commands & checks)
- Create new kv version: vault kv put secret/data/myapp cred=@new_creds.json metadata.rotation_job_id=RJOB-123
- List active policies for a token: vault token lookup -format=json | jq '.policies'
- Check last_rotation_ts metadata: vault kv get -format=json secret/data/db-admin | jq '.data.metadata.last_rotation_ts'
- Evidence push (curl): curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"rotation_job_id":"RJOB-123","changed_paths":["secret/data/db-admin"]}' https://evidence.redwood.internal/ingest

9) Appendix: policy and key naming conventions (short)
- Vault mount paths: secret/data/<team>/<service>
- Rotation job ids: RJOB-<YYYYMMDD>-<svc>-<seq>
- Evidence bundle ids: EB-<sha1prefix>
- RBAC role ids: role:<team>:<role>

10) Open action items
- (OWNED: Liam) Add automated smoke tests for all DB credential rotations by 2025-01-31.
- (OWNED: Sofia) Publish canonical RBAC-v2 -> Vault policy mapping to Confluence and link from Vault UI.
- (OWNED: DevOps) Add HSM-backed key usage telemetry into SIEM exports.

Contact & escalation
- Primary owner: Asha Patel (asha.patel@redwood.ai)
- On-call secops: see internal rota (linked in Confluence).
